{{short description|Russian mathematician (1903-1976)}}
{{family name hatnote|Nikolaevich|Bronshtein|lang=Eastern Slavic}}
{{use dmy dates|date=January 2022|cs1-dates=y}}
{{use list-defined references|date=January 2022}}
'''Ilya Nikolaevich Bronshtein''' ({{langx|ru|Илья Николаевич Бронштейн}}, {{langx|de|Ilja Nikolajewitsch Bronstein}}, also written as {{lang|de|Bronschtein}}; born 1903, died 1976) was a Russian [[applied mathematician]] and [[historian of mathematics]].

== Work and life ==
Bronshtein taught at the [[Moscow State Technical University]]<!-- Moscow State Engineering University --> (MAMI), then the State College of Mechanical Engineering, on the Chair of Advanced Mathematics established in 1939. He also collaborated at the [[Zhukovsky Central Aerohydrodynamic Institute]]<!-- N. E. Zhukovsky -->.

With [[Dmitrii Abramovich Raikov]], Bronshtein authored a Russian handbook on elementary mathematics, mechanics and physics ({{lang|ru|Справочник по елементарнои математике, механике и физике}}), which was published in 1943.<ref name="Bronshtein-Raikov_1943"/>

Bronshtein is known as the author of a handbook of mathematics for engineers and students of technical universities,<ref name="Ziegler_2002"/> which he wrote together with [[Konstantin Adolfovic Semendyayev]] around the 1939/1940 timeframe. [[Hot lead typesetting]] for the work had already started when the [[Siege of Leningrad]] prohibited further development and the [[print matrices]] were relocated.<ref name="Ziegler_2002"/> After the [[World War II|war]], they were first considered lost, but could be found again years later, so that the first edition of {{lang|ru|[[Справочник по математике для инженеров и учащихся втузов]]}} could finally be published in 1945.<ref name="Ziegler_2002"/><ref name="Girlich_2014"/> This was a major success and went through eleven editions in Russia and was translated into various languages, including German and English, until the publisher [[Nauka (publisher)|Nauka]] planned to replace it with a translation of the American [[Mathematical Handbook for Scientists and Engineers]] by [[Granino A. Korn|Granino]] and [[Theresa M. Korn]] in 1968.<ref name="Ziegler_2002"/><ref name="Girlich_2014"/>
However, in a parallel development starting in 1970, the so called "[[Bronshtein and Semendyayev]]" (BS), which had been translated into German in 1958, underwent a major overhaul by a team of [[East-Germany|East-German]] authors around Günter Grosche, Viktor & Dorothea Ziegler (of [[University of Leipzig]]), to which Bronshtein himself could no longer contribute due to reasons of age.<ref name="Ziegler_2002"/> This was published in 1979 and spawned translations into many other languages as well, including a retranslation into Russian and an English edition. In 1986, the 13th Russian edition was published. The German '[[Wende (GDR)|Wende]]' and the later [[German reunification|reunification]] led to considerable changes in the publishing environment in Germany between 1989 and 1991, which eventually resulted in two independent German publishing branches by [[Eberhard Zeidler (mathematician)|Eberhard Zeidler]] (published 1995–2013) and by {{ill|Gerhard Musiol|de}} & Heiner Mühlig (published 1992–2020) to expand and maintain the work up to the present, again with translations into many other languages including English.
